Quantum Capital: an interactive brief

⬇ Download the data (xlsx)
2002–2026 (2026 = Jan–Aug) · fixed FX · every chart drills down to the source: click a bar, then a company, then the record.
Method: click to expand
What this is. Every financing event and government program in the quantum computing industry that could be verified, 2002–2026. The download button above gives you the full dataset. Building and checking it took 2,437 research agents and ≈4.2 billion tokens of analysis.

What this does not cover. This tracks capital that companies raise. Several of the largest quantum programs in the world raise nothing, so they carry no dollars here: Google, Microsoft, Intel, Amazon, NVIDIA, IBM outside its government awards, NTT, Hitachi, Toshiba and Fujitsu all fund quantum from internal budgets that no filing separates from the rest of the business. They appear in the company lists, and they appear when they transact at arm's length, meaning government awards, acquisitions, and investments they make in others. Their internal spending is real and is not counted, because estimating it would mean inventing a number. China's state spending is excluded for the same reason. National program budgets are tracked separately in figure 3 rather than mixed into company capital.

How every number was checked: two independent steps.
1 · A research agent finds the figure in a primary source: an SEC or stock-exchange filing, a government award database, or the company's own announcement. 2 · A second, independent agent tries to refute it: re-deriving the amount at fixed exchange rates and testing it against every other event for double-counting. Only figures that survive both steps are shown. What counts as money. Cash that actually reached the company: after share redemptions, after fees. Announced headlines are not used: a "$400M" listing that delivered $96M after redemptions is shown as $96M. Program budgets ("up to $X") are never mixed into company capital. They are spread across their official spend periods and shown as their own series in figure 3, and figure 2's government band is the sum of that series and the money paid direct to companies.

Known limits, stated plainly. 216 of 975 events have undisclosed amounts, so every total is a floor. Government awards to companies in 2014–2019 are under-counted (US award databases limited access during collection). China's state spending is excluded as unquantifiable; disclosed Chinese company raises are included.

Data as of 11 August 2026

1Companies per modality

Hardware companies by modality. Click a slice, then a company.

Superconducting has the most companies. Trapped ion holds the most money with far fewer companies. Capital per company differs by more than ten times across modalities.

2Total capital by year

Before 2021 the sector raised a few hundred million dollars a year. SPAC listings caused the 2021 increase. Totals stayed flat 2022 to 2024. In 2025 the total quadrupled because listed companies sold new shares at higher prices. 2026 nearly matches 2025 in eight months. The green band of direct government money is new.

3Government money

A government announces a multi year budget once, so in the announcement view the full amount lands in one bar. The default view divides each program across its official period, verified for 76 of 89 programs. It shows the rate of government spending.

4Events each year: count, then composition

Chips filter bands. Click a bar for its events.

Event counts grow steadily: 3 in 2016, 24 in 2020, 92 in 2026. Few companies advance: 111 seed rounds become 92 Series A, 49 Series B, 15 Series C. Government money is the fastest growing band.

5Modality: ranked by total capital

Capital by modality. Click a bar, then a company.

Most trapped ion money is public market money from two listed companies. Its venture funding fell once those leaders went public. New venture money now goes to silicon spin and superconducting.

6Capital by country

Capital plus programs by country. The hatched band is China's unverifiable range.

US companies received about two thirds of the money. No other country reaches 10%. China's figure shows only what its system publishes, not what it spends.

7Quantum against the wider venture market

Quantum rounds are larger than the venture market at every stage, and the gap widens as companies mature. By Series C the quantum median runs off the right edge of the benchmark entirely.

Benchmark source: Carta, State of Startups 2025, covering January to October 2025. Bubble positions are transcribed from the published stage charts and are read to the nearest gridline, so treat them as close approximations rather than exact figures. Carta measures rounds executed on its own cap-table platform; our quantum figures come from this brief's own ledger. © 2025 eShares, Inc. dba Carta, Inc. All rights reserved.
